topic: sub:12|Relative frequency and probability|Number of outcomes for an experiment

parts.latex: A taxi number plate begins with a letter T and is followed by 4 digits. Each digit can be one of the numbers $0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8$ or $9$. How many different number plates of this type are there?

solutions.latex:
The plate begins with the fixed letter T, so there is only 1 choice for the first position.

Each of the 4 digits can be any of 10 digits, with repeats allowed.
$$1\times 10\times 10\times 10\times 10=10\times 10\times 10\times 10$$
Option A and option C do not allow repeated digits, and option D includes 26 choices for the letter, which is fixed.

$$\therefore\ 10\times 10\times 10\times 10 \text{ plates}$$

parts.latex:
Postcodes in Australia are made up of four digits e.g. 2040.

How many different postcodes beginning with 2 are possible?

solutions.latex:
The postcode has the form $2\_\_\_$, so the first digit is fixed.

Each of the other three places can be any of $10$ digits.

$$\begin{aligned} \text{Number} &= 10\times10\times10 \\ &= 1000 \end{aligned}$$

parts.latex:
A new issue of car registration plates is being designed. The new plates will display 2 digits then 2 alphabetical characters followed by another digit. All plates will then end with the letter N. Numbers and letters may be repeated.

An example is shown below.

\exfigure{495_q5_1}

Which of the following represents the number of possible number plates?

solutions.latex:
Number of choices for each position:
$$10,\ 10,\ 26,\ 26,\ 10,\ 1$$
The final letter N is fixed, so it gives only 1 choice.
$$\text{Number of plates} = 10^3\times 26^2$$
This is option C.

parts.latex:
Kate's online banking security code must contain two letters (A-Z) followed by two digits (0-9). Letters and digits can be repeated.

If Kate chooses a code starting with the letter B, which of the following expressions gives the correct number of possible codes?

solutions.latex:
The code has four positions: letter, letter, digit, digit.

The first letter is fixed as B, so it has $1$ choice.

The second letter has $26$ choices, and each digit has $10$ choices (repeats allowed).
$$1 \times 26 \times 10 \times 10 = 26 \times 10^2$$
Hence the correct option is C.
